VERIFIED SOURCES:
[SRC:CDRC2023-R7-FEE]
Source: Rule 7, Consumer Protection (Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions) (Amendment) Rules, 2023, G.S.R. 606(E)
Status: In force.
Official wording: Upto Rupees Five Lakh Nil | Above Rupees Five Lakh and upto Rupees Ten Lakh Rs. 200 | Above Rupees Ten Lakh and upto Rupees Twenty Lakh Rs. 400 | Above Rupees Twenty Lakh and upto Rupees Fifty Lakh Rs. 1000 | Above Rupees Fifty Lakh and upto Rupees One Crore Rs. 2000 | Above Rupees One Crore and upto Rupees Two Crore Rs. 2500
Plain explanation: The filing fee depends on the amount paid for the goods or services: no fee up to Rs. 5 lakh, Rs. 200 up to Rs. 10 lakh, Rs. 400 up to Rs. 20 lakh, Rs. 1,000 up to Rs. 50 lakh, Rs. 2,000 up to Rs. 1 crore and Rs. 2,500 up to Rs. 2 crore. Higher bands are in the rule. Check the fee shown on e-Jagriti before filing.

[SRC:CPA2019-S2-47-viii]
Source: Section 2(47)(viii), The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (35 of 2019)
Status: In force.
Official wording: refusing, after selling goods or rendering services, to take back or withdraw defective goods or to withdraw or discontinue deficient services and to refund the consideration thereof, if paid, within the period stipulated in the bill or cash memo or receipt or in the absence of such stipulation, within a period of thirty days
Plain explanation: Refusing to take back defective goods, or to stop deficient services, and refund the money is listed as an unfair trade practice. The time limit is the period stated in the bill or receipt. If none is stated, it is thirty days.

[SRC:ECOM2020-R6-3]
Source: Rule 6(3), Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, G.S.R. 462(E)
Status: In force.
Official wording: No seller offering goods or services through a marketplace e -commerce entity shall refuse to take back goods, or withdraw or discontinue services purchased or agreed to be purchased, or refuse to refund consideration, if paid, if such goods or services are defective, deficient or spurious, or if the goods or services are not of the characteristics or features as advertised or as agreed to, or if such goods or services are delivered late from the stated delivery schedule | Provided that in the case of late delivery, this sub -rule shall not be applied if such late delivery was due to force majeure
Plain explanation: A marketplace seller must not refuse to take back goods or refund the money if the goods or services are defective, deficient, spurious, different from what was advertised or agreed, or delivered late. Late delivery caused by force majeure is an exception.

[SRC:ECOM2026-COMMENCEMENT]
Source: Rule 1(2), Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026, G.S.R. 789(E)
Status: In force.
Official wording: They shall come into force with effect from 1st January, 2027.
Plain explanation: The 2026 amendment to the E-Commerce Rules starts on 1 January 2027. Until then, the earlier wording applies.

[SRC:ECOM2020-R4-10]
Source: Rule 4(10), Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, G.S.R. 462(E)
Status: In force.
Official wording: Every e-commerce entity shall effect all payments towards accepted refund requests of the consumers as prescribed by the Reserve Bank of India or any other competent authority under any law for the time being in force, within a reasonable period of time, or as prescribed under applicable laws
Plain explanation: Once a refund request is accepted, an online platform must pay it within a reasonable time, or within the time set by the Reserve Bank of India or other applicable law. This rule does not itself state a fixed number of days.

[SRC:JUR2021-R3]
Source: Rule 3, Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of the District Commission, the State Commission and the National Commission) Rules, 2021, G.S.R. 912(E)
Status: In force.
Official wording: the District Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration does not exceed fifty lakh rupees
Plain explanation: The District Commission hears complaints where the amount paid for the goods or services is up to fifty lakh rupees. This replaced the higher limit originally written in section 34 of the Act.

[SRC:CPA2019-S35-1]
Source: Section 35(1), The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (35 of 2019)
Status: In force.
Official wording: Provided that the complaint under this sub -section may be filed electronically in such manner as may be prescribed | A complaint, in relation to any goods sold or delivered or agreed to be sold or delivered or any service provided or agreed to be provided, may be filed with a District Commission by
Plain explanation: A consumer can file a complaint about goods or services with a District Commission, and the Act allows complaints to be filed electronically.

[SRC:CPA2019-S2-28]
Source: Section 2(28), The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (35 of 2019)
Status: In force.
Official wording: gives a false guarantee to, or is likely to mislead the consumers as to the nature, substance, quantity or quality of such product or service | falsely describes such product or service | deliberately conceals important information
Plain explanation: An advertisement can be misleading if it falsely describes a product or service, gives a false guarantee, is likely to mislead about its nature or quality, or deliberately hides important information.

[SRC:ECOM2026-R4-5]
Source: Rule 4(5), Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026, G.S.R. 789(E)
Status: NOT YET IN FORCE. Starts on 2027-01-01.
Official wording: acknowledges the receipt of any consumer complaint within forty -eight hours, provides the complainant with a copy of the complaint as recorded by the grievance officer and redresses the complaint within one month from the date of receipt of the complaint
Plain explanation: From 1 January 2027, the grievance officer must also give the complainant a copy of the complaint as recorded. The forty-eight hour and one month limits stay the same.

[SRC:ECOM2020-R4-5]
Source: Rule 4(5), Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, G.S.R. 462(E)
Status: In force.
Official wording: Every e-commerce entity shall ensure that the grievance officer referred to in sub -rule (4) acknowledges the receipt of any consumer complaint within forty -eight hours and redresses the complaint within one month from the date of receipt of the complaint
Plain explanation: A platform's grievance officer must acknowledge a consumer complaint within forty-eight hours and redress it within one month of receiving it.
